corrections.caveats: First-party measurement: the author of Arduino_GFX ran all four libraries, and his README says 'This library is not putting speed at the first priority'. The README table does not link its code, but the sketches and raw output are in moononournation/Arduino_graphicstest_PDQ (result.txt matches the table digit for digit; the units are microseconds per the sketches' 'Benchmark micro-secs' header). The four sketches run identical test bodies (adapted from Adafruit and Xark's PDQ graphicstest) at the same 240x320 resolution, RGB565 colour and 40 MHz SPI, with no DMA and no bus held across tests; Arcs are N/A for Adafruit_GFX and TFT_eSPI because those libraries lacked arc calls at the time. Single pass per test, no repeat count or variance; library versions not recorded, and an earlier 2020-10-15 run in the same repository's README gives different numbers for some libraries (for example TFT_eSPI Lines 308,601), so results move with library versions. The benchmark repository's README still lists the older hardware (ESP32-DevKitC, ESP32 LCDKit, Arduino IDE 1.8.13). Compiler flags and Arduino board-menu settings are not stated. Screen fill is bound by the SPI link: five full-screen fills of 240x320x16 bits at 40 MHz need 153,600 microseconds (derived from page data), so fills differ only in overhead above that wire limit. Weak category fit: an embedded SPI display driver stack with drawing primitives, not a general path rasterizer comparable to Skia, Cairo or Blend2D. license.txt is the Adafruit two-clause BSD text, so BSD-2-Clause is recorded; the GitHub sidebar does not detect a license.

corrections.caveats: Measured by the author of a competing library (Arduino_GFX), not by the LovyanGFX project; the result is against that author's interest since LovyanGFX beats Arduino_GFX on most rows. The README table does not link its code, but the sketches and raw output are in moononournation/Arduino_graphicstest_PDQ (result.txt matches the table; units are microseconds). The LovyanGFX sketch runs the identical test body as the Adafruit_GFX, Arduino_GFX and TFT_eSPI sketches at the same 240x320 resolution, RGB565 colour and 40 MHz SPI, with no DMA and no bus held across tests (panel rotation 2 versus 0 for the others, same portrait size). Single pass per test, no repeat count or variance; the LovyanGFX version used is not recorded and an earlier 2020-10-15 run gives slightly different numbers (Lines 261,781). Compiler flags and Arduino board-menu settings are not stated. Screen fill is bound by the SPI link: five full-screen fills of 240x320x16 bits at 40 MHz need 153,600 microseconds (derived from page data), and LovyanGFX's 154,341 sits at that limit. LovyanGFX's own examples/Test/TFT_graphicstest_PDQ sketch differs (it holds the bus with startWrite and divides fill time by 5), so its own output is not comparable to this table. Weak category fit: an embedded SPI/parallel display driver stack with drawing primitives, not a general path rasterizer comparable to Skia, Cairo or Blend2D. license.txt collects several permissive notices (FreeBSD two-clause for LovyanGFX and the TFT_eSPI parts, Adafruit BSD, MIT); the README lists further components under MIT, 3-clause BSD and the IPA Font License for converted IPA fonts; BSD-2-Clause is recorded as the main library license.
